quote_text:
Listen, bitterly disappointed. I think everyone  can see how much we put into the game and we  
obviously get ourselves into a real good position  at halftime. You believe that there's always going  
to be some sort of fallout from Rangers' point of  view—you know there's going to be a reaction. And  
I probably, I just said to the players there,  I never want to be a glorious loser, so I don't  
want to sit here in front of anybody and start to  make excuses or, you know, start to pat ourselves  
on the back because we get to this stage. It's  been a good achievement to get here, but we just  
felt that in moments in the game we probably just  lacked that wee bit of composure and a wee bit  
better decision making. I think the second goal's  symptomatic of that. Second goal Rangers get,  
well, probably, well, it's a foul on Zak Rudden,  I think, which the referee's maybe acknowledged at  
the time, but he stays on his feet, tries to keep  the ball alive, and it's possibly just at a spell  
in the game where if we manage it better and make  a slightly better decision—no criticism of Zak,  
he's too honest at times—but I just felt that that  was one that led to a square pass and obviously  
the break and the counter-attack at that stage  for Rangers. And from our own point of view,  
I think we just have to look to improve slightly  on the ball. That'll be the bit that would get us  
over this hurdle. That's not a criticism;  that's what we want to try and evolve to.  
But in the next stage for us, off the back of  what is a sore one today, is just to try and  
pick the players up because we don't want a  hangover off the back of a disappointing day.
Possibly. I think you guys were all sitting here;  I think the environment and the atmosphere at  
that time goes a little bit negative against  Rangers because they find themselves behind,  
because, you know, generally nobody expects that  to be the case and considering some of the chat  
before the game and what we've heard midweek. But  yeah, and that's probably what I'm alluding to,  
just those areas. No criticism individually; I  hate finger pointers, I hate people that just  
start to saddle that blame on one person, but  just making a better decision sometimes for us.  
And I felt we were too quick to try and create  an attack and we probably could have strung more  
passes together and ring-fenced attack. So  these are all bits we'll try and learn from;  
these are all bits that we'll try and improve on.  Second time we've played Rangers here, and to be  
honest we had a very, very similar feel. And we've  had a good start to the season, so I'm not going  
to be sitting here criticizing the players because  when you see them slump to their knees at the end,  
that wasn't disappointment, that was exhaustion.  They've put so much in, so I can't ask any more  
from them in that front, but for us to try and  look to create more chances and retain the ball,  
I think we just probably have to work that wee  bit more on that and I'll try and drive that.
Yeah, I've said so many times we've got so many  good stories. In goal, Matty Connelly—he's had  
three senior starts in football and they've been  in the last seven days: Celtic, Dundee United at  
Tannadice, and Rangers in the semi-final. And you  can't buy those experiences; you can't buy how  
that feels as a young player, which he is. Ewan  Wilson, but obviously the massive story is that  
we've got the youngest captain in our club's  history in Lennon Miller at 16. He earned it,  
he's merited it, and again I thought he took  that responsibility on his shoulders today.  
He'll critique himself and realize there's times  where he can get better, but I've just been asked  
the question a minute or two ago, how does that  set them up for the rest of their career. I'm  
jealous of them to get those experiences so young  and so early in your career, the infancy of your  
career. I think it's just a brilliant, brilliant  thing and that's what we want to continue to try  
to do as a football club—try and bring through  our own. Ewan Wilson coming back from being  
juniors to play that at Hampden in a semi-final  out of position in the middle of the park,  
and it's not a bad experience to have and I'm  sure that they'll improve off the back of here.
Yeah, I understand I'm not going to hammer  referees here at all. I thought Nick Walsh  
was really good in the game today; I thought he  handled it well, I thought he allowed a flow to  
the game as best he could. I just felt that at the  time the center back's manhandling our striker,  
he's trying to be honest to stay on his feet  and to try and retain the ball, and it's the  
one that we all speak about sometimes—to  let your team breathe, do you have to fall  
down for it to be a foul? I think what Nick's  done is allowed the game to try and roll on;  
it goes to Dan Casey, but that also leans back  to the point that I'm saying—not a finger point  
at Dan—but we play him out of position,  he's now playing in a wide area for us,  
and he looks to play a square pass, Rangers  turn it over. And so as always there's an  
honesty in what we do and that honesty leads  back to trying to make those improvements and  
make better decisions. So as it ends up, an  attack for Motherwell, a goal for Rangers.
I don't know that we've shown it plenty over a  spell. I spoke about, you know, sitting here this  
time last year and we were on a bad run and we  were playing some unbelievable football at times,  
and our ball possession was very good, our  chances created was very good. And for us  
as a football club it's just trying to find a  balance between what we do. Sometimes there,  
you know, saw a game yesterday which was a wee  bit of warrior stuff—sometimes you're going to  
have to take part in those games in this league.  But I just think here in a big open space and  
the big pitch at Hampden sometimes we need to  try and utilize that a wee bit more and have a  
little bit more patience and composure to what  we do. Absolutely no criticism of the players;  
it's just that I always believe in trying to get  better myself but for them and the football club.
I would have loved the six subs because I  felt that myself—we had to make changes:  
Stephen O'Donnell coming off, Matty Connelly  coming off, we had to make an adjustment in  
the middle of the park and we had to make a  change at center back. So if you can try and  
speak to somebody and see if you get me  six or seven subs, that would be great.
Absolutely, yeah, but the circumstances  that come about, I would love to have got  
Mikael Mandron on the pitch, I'd love to  have got Tony Watt, and by the time the  
end of the game comes and you've got  Dan Casey up the park because he's got  
an eye for a goal to be fair to him and  he can be quite adventurous that way.
Of course I do, but the circumstances have  led us to the point where we couldn't get  
any more strikers on the pitch, but have a look  at all games that we've played and we've chased,  
we've ended up with four and  five strikers on the pitch,  
so it's not something that  I'm not accustomed to doing.
Alright, thank you.
title: Stuart Kettlewell FULL Post Match Press Conference | Motherwell 1-2 Rangers
